episodes.title: Paderborn KAt bearing test rig - outer-race damage (EDM)

diagnosis.summary: At 900 rpm, the pattern of feature ratios matches the outer-race reference signature for this operating point almost exactly. The sharp drop in low-frequency and shaft-harmonic energy plus higher kurtosis does not look like unbalance, misalignment or a load change. At 900 rpm a bearing defect is only weakly visible, so I am asking for a 1500 rpm test to confirm. If it is an outer-race defect, high-frequency energy should rise sharply there.

causes.evidence: Observed ratios match the outer-race reference at N09_M07_F10 (observed vs reference): rms 0.836 vs 0.833, kurt 1.62 vs 1.7, b0 0.0776 vs 0.083, b1 0.12 vs 0.12, b2 1.39 vs 1.33, b3 0.656 vs 0.649, bhf 0.603 vs 0.607, a1x 0.277 vs 0.284, app 0.264 vs 0.288, cur_rms 1.03 vs 1.03.
Kurtosis is up (13.93, ratio 1.62) and b2 is up (ratio 1.39), which points to impacts. There is no inner-race reference signature to compare against, so an inner-race defect cannot be ruled out.
Same impact signs (kurt 1.62, b2 1.39). There is no reference signature for this fault either.
Levels fall unevenly: b0 is 0.078, but b2 rises to 1.39 and kurt to 1.62. A mounting problem would shift all bands by about the same amount, so this is unlikely.
Ruled out by the data: 1x and 2x shaft amplitudes are low, not high (a1x 0.277, a2x 0.277). Current is normal (cur_rms 1.03), so a load change is also unlikely.

diagnosis.test_rationale: This is the same load and radial force at the higher speed, and its outer-race reference has the clearest signature: rms 2.55, bhf 7.33, b3 2.84, kurt 2.71, with a1x still around 0.33. If those appear, the bearing is confirmed. If levels stay roughly the same or low, the cause is more likely a sensor/mounting problem or a different fault.
diagnosis.action: Plan to inspect and replace the test bearing on the drive shaft. Before that, check the outer-race defect frequency (BPFO) in the envelope spectrum and keep an eye on bearing temperature.

diagnosis.summary: This matches the outer-race bearing defect reference signature at both operating points tested. At 900 rpm the bearing hides the fault: overall rms drops (ratio 0.836) while kurtosis rises (1.62). At 1500 rpm under 1000 N load the high-frequency bearing band rises sharply: bhf 7.35x and b3 2.86x healthy, with rms 2.55x and kurtosis 2.71x. Current is normal, so the load did not change. Shaft-speed components (a1x/a2x) are low, which rules out unbalance and misalignment.

causes.evidence: At N15_M07_F10 the observed ratios nearly equal the outer-race reference. Observed vs reference: rms 2.55 vs 2.55, kurt 2.71 vs 2.71, bhf 7.35 vs 7.33, b3 2.86 vs 2.84, b2 1.55 vs 1.53, b0 0.0977 vs 0.107, a1x 0.317 vs 0.325. At N09_M07_F10 they match too: rms 0.836 vs 0.833, b0 0.0776 vs 0.083, b1 0.12 vs 0.12, b2 1.39 vs 1.33, bhf 0.603 vs 0.607. bhf rises 19.3x from 900 to 1500 rpm.
The high-frequency pattern is also bearing-like (bhf 7.35, kurt 14.74), but there is no inner-race reference signature to compare against. The outer-race fit is near-exact.
The broadband rise in b3 (2.86) and bhf (7.35) is also consistent with a rolling-element fault, but no reference signature is available for it.
Unlikely: the changes do not shift all bands equally. b0 is at 0.0977 while bhf is at 7.35, and the level depends strongly on speed.

diagnosis.test_rationale: The 1500 rpm test matched the outer-race signature on every feature, so confidence is 0.9 or higher and no further test is needed.
diagnosis.action: Schedule a replacement of the drive-shaft test bearing (outer-race defect) and check the removed bearing's outer race for spalling. Until then, run below 1500 rpm and limit radial load where possible.

episodes.title: CubeMars RI60 PMSM fault rig (Zenodo 22039010) - magnet fault (demagnetisation)

diagnosis.summary: At 500 rpm the vibration rise is concentrated in b1 (6.96x) and b2 (3.81x). rms is 1.76x, crest is low at 0.603 and kurtosis is normal at 0.942. This best matches the magnet-demagnetisation signature at 500 rpm. Eccentricity is the second candidate. Bearing and stator signatures do not fit.

causes.evidence: Observed vs magnet reference at 500 rpm: rms 1.76 vs 1.88, crest 0.603 vs 0.703, kurt 0.942 vs 0.909, b0 1.86 vs 1.84, b3 1.76 vs 2.19, a1x 1.77 vs 1.28, a2x 1.46 vs 1.3. b1 is the dominant band (6.96, reference 27.2), but its size is below the reference and b2 is above it (3.81 vs 1.88).

Eccentricity reference at 500 rpm: rms 2.06, b2 2.71, a1x 1.78 and a2x 1.69 are close to the observed 1.76, 3.81, 1.77 and 1.46. However, the reference b3 of 6.4 is far above the observed 1.76, and the reference b1 of 2.12 is far below the observed 6.96.

Stator reference at 500 rpm is almost flat (rms 1.05, b1 1.28, b2 0.59), which does not match the observed rms 1.76 and b2 3.81. Stator faults can look different at other speeds, so it is not ruled out.
No reference matches the observed b1 6.96 / b2 3.81 ratio exactly.
The rise is not uniform across bands (b1 6.96 vs b3 1.76) or axes (z 2.64 vs x 1.52), which argues against a mounting fault.

diagnosis.test_rationale: At 1000 rpm the two leading hypotheses diverge most. The eccentricity reference predicts b0 about 37x, b3 about 52x, a1x about 8.8x and rms about 5.7x. The magnet reference predicts b0 about 2.4x, b3 about 6.9x, a1x about 1.4x, and b1 and b2 about 13x and 24x. The 750 rpm separation is weaker (b3 28 vs 5.7, a1x 4.1 vs 1.6).
diagnosis.action: Run the 1000 rpm test to confirm the cause. If magnet demagnetisation is confirmed, plan a back-EMF or flux check of the rotor magnets. If eccentricity is confirmed, plan an air-gap and rotor alignment inspection.

diagnosis.summary: The ratio patterns at both 500 and 1000 rpm closely match the magnet_demagnetisation reference signature. The test at 1000 rpm gives a near-exact match: rms 3.99 vs ref 3.85, b1 15.8 vs 13.5, b2 25.4 vs 24.1, b3 7.07 vs 6.93, b0 2.98 vs 2.39, a1x 1.6 vs 1.41, a2x 1.62 vs 1.57 and app 0.996 vs 0.763. At 500 rpm the level also fits: rms 1.76 vs 1.88, crest 0.603 vs 0.703, b0 1.86 vs 1.84 and b3 1.76 vs 2.19, with mid-band energy (b1 6.96) leading. Bearing, eccentricity and stator patterns do not fit. The fault is stable over 8 windows (rms 0.2558 to 0.2555). The kurtosis spike at 1000 rpm (kurt 11.3, peak 6.7) is treated as a recording glitch, as the machine notes advise.

causes.evidence: Overall level grows with speed (rms 1.76 to 3.99), but 1x does not: a1x 1.6 at 1000 vs ref 8.82, b0 2.98 vs ref 37, b3 7.07 vs ref 52
Fault is absent or weak at 500 in the ref (b2 0.59), but observed b2 is 3.81 at 500 and 25.4 at 1000 vs ref 2.15
Ref ratios are far larger (1000: b3 421, b2 249, rms 17.7) than observed (b3 7.07, b2 25.4, rms 3.99); kurt 11.3 is likely a glitch
Rise is not uniform across bands (b1 6.96 vs b0 1.86 at 500), and the z_rms ratio drops from 2.64 to 1.46 with speed, so the pattern does not look like a loose mount

diagnosis.test_rationale: The top hypothesis is at 0.85 after matching two operating points against the references, so a 750 rpm test would not change the ranking.
diagnosis.action: Schedule rotor inspection: measure back-EMF per phase against the healthy baseline to confirm magnet flux loss. Plan a rotor or magnet replacement, and meanwhile avoid running at high speed and overheating, which speed up demagnetisation.
